heading: INT. OPERA HOUSE COURTHOUSE - JUDGE'S CHAMBERS (FORMER GREEN ROOM) - DAY

units.text: INT. OPERA HOUSE COURTHOUSE - JUDGE'S CHAMBERS (FORMER GREEN ROOM) - DAY
A faded theatrical dressing room turned into judicial chambers.
Mirrors ringed with dead bulbs.
A costume rack stuffed with law books.
A velvet couch.
A desk made from an old stage trunk.
Light slants through dust.
JUDGE AUGUSTINE PEREIRA, 60s, silver beard, half-robed, stands at the window looking at the empty orchestra pit below.
HELEN OSEI, 40s, state prosecutor, sensible suit, notes in hand, sits on the edge of the couch.
RUFUS KLEIN, 50s, defense counsel, bow tie askew, stands by the door, slowly turning his briefcase by its handle.
Counselors. Thank you for coming on short notice.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Your Honor.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: Your Honor, I assumed it was urgent.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: It is. A juror was found at six this morning in the third box. Asleep. Under a blanket. With a lunch pail.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Asleep?
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Asleep and unwilling to give an account of how he got there.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: The jury was sequestered at a hotel.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: It was.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Then how did he...
units.name: OSEI

units.text: Ms. Osei, I too would like to know how a juror escaped a hotel and arrived at an opera house at midnight.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Your Honor, I'd like to know whether he's in any condition to serve.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: He appears sound.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Appears.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Mr. Klein, a man who sleeps in an opera box is not necessarily mad.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Your Honor, with respect, he is a man who sleeps in an opera box.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Your Honor, the state does not consent to a mistrial.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: The defense does.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Of course it does.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: Ms. Osei, the state's case is in trouble and you know it.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: My case is fine.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: Your witness identified my client as Tuesday's man. The crime was on a Wednesday.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: A clerical error.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: A fatal error.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Counselors.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: They both stop.
The Judge turns from the window.
I have a proposal. Ms. Osei, amend your complaint to the Wednesday. Mr. Klein, stipulate the juror's competence. We proceed. Tomorrow. Eleven o'clock.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: And if I decline?
units.name: OSEI

units.text: Then I declare a mistrial myself, and the state starts over in eighteen months.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Eighteen months. In this economy.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Mr. Klein.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: Sorry, Judge.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Your Honor, you've left the state very little room.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: Ms. Osei, I've left you precisely as much room as the theater left me.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: She almost smiles.
Klein opens his mouth, closes it.
Wednesday.
units.name: OSEI

units.text: Stipulated.
units.name: KLEIN

units.text: Then we are adjourned.
units.name: PEREIRA

units.text: They file out.
Pereira picks up a dusty costume crown from the rack, regards it for a long moment, and sets it gently on the trunk beside the gavel.
